title: Right-click does what you would expect, everywhere on the timeline
goal: A person expects to right-click a clip, a cut, a track or the scrub bar and find the actions for that thing, rather than hunting for a tool or a panel button. Put those menus in, carrying what the mock and a Premiere editor would expect.
notes:
Intake detail (the goal as first filed, moved here by triage 2026-09-23): User: 'we need a right click menu on a segment. I expect to not need to have tools for everything, but that you can right click on places to reveal actions that can be taken at the scrub bar, or for the clip'. Target: the user's mocks (docs/design/mocks/pages/video.html, video-shell.html, comp-video.html and the page named here) at their fidelity; runner-prompt rules on default config, side-by-side with the mock, labels-not-explanations and right-click apply. Ask throughout: would a Premiere editor get this, and is it easier here?

Filed from the 2026-09-23 video audit in the intake window.
acceptance: Clip: Split at Playhead, Delete, Ripple Delete, Detach Audio, Speed submenu, Freeze Frame, Add Transition, Rename, Reveal in Finder, Duplicate
Cut/edit point: Add Transition submenu, Remove Transition, Roll Edit
Track header: Rename, Add Track Above/Below, Hide/Mute, Lock, Group, Delete Track
Scrub bar and ruler: Add Marker, Set In, Set Out, Clear In/Out, Split Everything Here
Canvas over a video layer: the layer's actions plus Split at Playhead
Every item also has its Premiere shortcut shown in the menu

log.note: triage 2026-09-23: goal rewritten in plain language, the old one kept at the top of notes

video-shell.html was deleted on 2026-09-23 (task the-video-mocks-are-the-user-s-again-and-d18-is): it was the loop's own study arguing against tracks. The target is now pages/video.html, the video-*.html walkthroughs and comp-video.html, restored as the user drew them, plus UX-PATTERNS D18 (rewritten: a document with time has tracks). Where this task mentions video-shell, read video.html.

from the linked-sound task (2026-09-23): a first clip right-click menu exists now, TimelineClipMenu in ClipPiecesBar.swift, on picture clips and on their linked sound segments: Detach Audio (when there is sound to detach), Split at Playhead, Delete. Extend it there rather than starting a second menu.

Adversarial pass before building. (1) The mock draws no right-click menus; the acceptance list is the spec, and video-cut-wt's command menu fixes three names and keys: Split at playhead B, Detach audio ⌃⇧D, Ripple delete ⌥⌫. (2) The app has no markers and no In/Out on the document timeline, so the ruler menu would be hollow: building a small core model here (markers + in/out, drawn on the ruler and as the transport scrubber's in/out marks the mock already draws) rather than shipping rows that do nothing. Export honouring In/Out is a separate follow-up. (3) Roll Edit from a menu has no gesture to drive, so it is Premiere's own menu verb: Roll Edit to Playhead (Extend Edit, E). (4) Shortcuts: a menu only prints a key the app honours. M, I, O, E conflict with Photoshop tool keys and the premiere-keys task owns timeline-focus routing, so those rows print no key until that lands (noted on that task). Keys wired here where free: ⌥⌫ ripple delete, ⌃⇧D detach, ⌥X clear in/out, ⇧⌘K split everything. (5) A Premiere editor right-clicks a clip and expects it picked: SwiftUI context menus cannot pick on open, so each row picks the piece it was opened on before acting.

Built: clip menu (Split at Playhead B, Freeze Frame, Speed submenu, Add Transition submenu at both ends of the piece, Detach Audio ⌃⇧D, Rename inline on the bar, Duplicate ⌘J, Reveal in Finder, Delete ⌫, Ripple Delete ⌥⌫; a clip on a locked track offers Unlock Track instead); cut menu on the join grip and the band (Add Transition, Remove Transition, Roll Edit to Playhead); track header Add Track Above/Below; ruler and scrub bar menu acting where you right-clicked (Add/Remove Marker, Set In, Set Out, Clear In and Out ⌥X, Split Everything Here ⇧⌘K, Clear All Markers) with markers (amber tabs) and In/Out (green wash + brackets on the ruler, green marks on the scrub bar as the mock draws); canvas layer menu gains Split at Playhead on a clip. Core: TimelineMarks.swift, TimelineMenuEdits.swift (ripple delete, split every clip, roll a cut), 18 tests. Video menu bar gets the same rows and keys; Hold This Frame renamed Freeze Frame to match the freeze mock. Found and fixed on the way: a SwiftUI context menu added after .offset hangs on the un-offset layout frame, so piece menus answered for the wrong piece and the join menu never opened; menus now go before the offset. Verified: Scripts/test.sh 9363 tests green; timeline-right-click-walk at defaults (no flags) ok with 16 real captures; 17 neighbouring clip/track/transition walks ok. Left rough (logged, not filed): the ruler's 'here' comes from hover, which the walk harness cannot drive, so the walk drags the playhead there first; open menus photograph clipped at the screen's bottom edge in the harness. Filed: export-and-playback-keep-to-the-in-and-out-marks (p2), find-out-whether-the-layer-menu-promises-a-dupli (p2). Folded key follow-up into premiere-s-keys-work-on-the-timeline.

Right-click menus on clip, join, track header, ruler, scrub bar and canvas-over-a-clip, with Premiere names and the keys the app honours; markers and In/Out added to the document; Ripple Delete, Split Everything, Roll Edit to Playhead in core with 18 tests. Verified by Scripts/test.sh (9363 green), timeline-right-click-walk at Next defaults (ok, 16 real captures) and 17 neighbouring walks. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-23-right-click-menus.json.
